title: Percent-escaped password in URL userinfo
summary: A synthetic https URL whose userinfo password contains percent-escapes (an escaped at-sign, colon and slash).
rationale: The password is the data after the first colon in userinfo. In the original text the escapes are literal bytes of the span: the expected extent covers the escaped form exactly as written, not a decoded form, so decoded-source mapping is a downstream evaluator concern (related encoding semantics: #94). An escaped at-sign must not end the userinfo early.

expectation.rationale: Flag, with the password as written (percent-escapes included) as the extent. RFC 3986 deprecates the userinfo password form and says applications should not render as clear text any data after the first colon; percent-encoded octets are written as %HH triplets (section 2.1). This is a standards statement, not a provider issuer statement.

sources.supports: Use of the format "user:password" in the userinfo field is deprecated. Applications should not render as clear text any data after the first colon.
A percent-encoded octet is encoded as a character triplet: % followed by two hexadecimal digits.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited provider and RFC pages read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. Product masking envelopes, decoded-source mapping and action policy stay with the downstream repositories.
